title: TrackFlow telemetry event schemas
description: Validate an event in two steps: it must match #/definitions/envelope, then the schema at #/events/<event_type>, which re-applies the envelope, fixes the event_type and allowlists the properties. Unknown properties are rejected (additionalProperties: false). Custom x-* keywords are documentation for humans and for the pipeline; validators ignore them.

verbs.created: a business record was persisted (after the commit, never before)
verbs.rejected: the system refused a request because of validation or a business rule
verbs.denied: the system refused a request because the caller is not authorised (HTTP 403)
verbs.triggered: a configured rule fired (for example a stock minimum was crossed)
verbs.detected: the system observed a condition on its own (an audit, a scan, an integrity check)
verbs.failed: something that should have worked did not (an attempt or a delivery)
verbs.returned: an operation answered with an error status
verbs.recorded: a measurement was taken (latency, load time)
verbs.requested: someone asked for something that completes later (password reset link)
verbs.completed: a multi-step process reached its end
verbs.changed: an existing record moved from one value to another
verbs.expired: a time-limited thing ran out (a session)
verbs.started: a guided task or a process began
verbs.abandoned: a guided task was left unfinished
verbs.analyzed: a file went through the analysis

eventId.description: Unique id of this event. Lets the pipeline drop duplicates when a batch is retried.

timestamp.description: When the thing happened, taken on the producer, for example `2026-11-21T14:03:22.418Z`. Always UTC with a `Z`.

sessionId.description: One browser session (created at sign-in, regenerated at sign-out). `null` only for events with no user session (service start, scheduled scans).

userId.description: Internal account id (`User.user_id`). It is pseudonymous: no name, no email. `null` for anonymous callers (failed logins) and system events.

event_type.description: Event name in `entity_action` format (lowercase snake case, entity first, then the verb from the controlled list).

schemaVersion.description: Version of the schema this event follows, for example `1.0.0`.

requestId.description: Correlation id. The frontend creates one per user action and sends it as `X-Request-ID`; the API reuses it, or creates one when absent, and writes it on every event of that request. For events with no request, a fresh UUID.

properties.description: Event-specific payload. Only the keys allowlisted for that `event_type` are accepted.

user_role.description: Role of the user who signed in.

method.description: How the user authenticated. Only `password` exists today; the field keeps the schema stable if single sign-on is added.

failures_before_success.description: Failed attempts for this account in the previous 15 minutes.

is_first_login.description: Whether this is the first sign-in of the account.

login_failed.x-statement: We capture login_failed because we need to know whether failed sign-ins are forgotten passwords or an attack (many attempts, or many different accounts), which allows us to make the decision enable rate limiting or account lockout, block abusive sources, or force password resets.

email_hash.description: Keyed hash of the email that was tried, to count attempts per account without storing the address.
email_hash.x-sanitization: First 16 hex characters of HMAC-SHA256(lowercased email, TELEMETRY_PEPPER). The pepper is a secret kept outside the repository.

source_network_hash.description: Keyed hash of the caller's network (IPv4 truncated to /24, IPv6 to /48), to spot one source trying many accounts.
source_network_hash.x-sanitization: First 16 hex characters of HMAC-SHA256(truncated address, TELEMETRY_PEPPER). The raw address is never stored. Retention 30 days.

attempts_in_window.description: Failed attempts for this email hash in the last 15 minutes, including this one.
